title: Methods Paper Using Household Survey Data to Identify Food Security Patterns in Uganda
author: Jannike Wichern
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vb6e2re

steps.title: Perform Household Level Food Availability Analysis
steps.instruction: Calculate food availability and contributing activities using household survey data and provided R-scripts.

substeps.instruction: Download 2010/11 Uganda household survey data from the World Bank (http://microdata.worldbank.org/index.php/catalog/2166).
Adjust file sources in scripts LSMS_Tools.R and LSMS_201011_param.R to enable the execution of script 1.4_LSMS_201011_IA.R.
Utilize the two provided CSV parameter files in LSMS_201011_param.R.

Run the following R-scripts: 1.1_LSMS201011_HHinfo_281016.R, 1.2_LSMS_201011_Crop_281016.R, 1.2a_LSMS_201011_Calculate_median_cropPrices_281016.R, 1.3_LSMS_201011_Lvst_281016.R, 1.3a_LSMS_201011_Calculate_median_livestockPrices_281016.R, 1.4_LSMS_201011_IA_281016.R, 1.5_LSMS_201011_Calc_contribution_crop_lvst_281016.R, LSMS_201011_param_281016.R, and LSMS_Tools_281016.R.

steps.title: Prepare Data for Regression Analysis
steps.instruction: Prepare household and spatial data layers for regression using the output from Step 1 and specific spatial datasets.

substeps.instruction: Acquire the following spatial data: Climate data (BioClim v1.4, http://www.worldclim.org/), Elevation (Jarvis et al. 2008, http://www.cgiar-csi.org/data), Soil data (Hengl et al. 2017), Population (Worldpop 2015, Worldpop.org.uk), Market access (Nelson 2008, http://forobs.jrc.ec.europa.eu/products/gam/download.php), and Length of growing period (HarvestChoice 2015, Harvestchoice.org).
Randomly off-set LSMS household locations using script 2.1.Random_coordinate_offset_081116.R.
Calculate soil carbon stock using script 2.2.soil_carbon_stock.R.
Sample spatial layers to the off-set household locations using script 2.3.Resampling_res_sample_spatial_to_point_5arcmin_180611.R.

steps.title: Conduct Regression Analysis
steps.instruction: Build regression models for variables of interest using spatial variables from Step 2 and household variables from Step 1.

substeps.instruction: Use a multiple inflated beta regression model (MIBR) for applicable variables (e.g., using script 3.1.MIBR_Banana_5arcmin_180612.R for banana contribution).
Use a multiple linear regression model (MLR) for applicable variables (e.g., using script 3.2.MLR_FoodAvail_5arcmin_180611.R for food availability).

steps.title: Perform Spatial Interpolation
steps.instruction: Spatially interpolate the variable of interest based on the regression model type used in Step 3.

substeps.instruction: For MIBR models, perform interpolation using script 4.1.MIBR_Banana_PART2_5arcmin_180612.R.
For MLR models, perform interpolation using script 4.2.MLR_FoodAvail_PART2_5arcmin_180611.R.
